title: Weak homotopy equivalences glue over a binary open cover
statement: Use the continuous cubical homotopy groups and path components of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: for any topological space $Z$ and $z\in Z$, $\pi_n(Z,z)$, $n\geq1$, consists of continuous maps $([0,1]^n,\partial[0,1]^n)\to(Z,z)$ modulo homotopy relative to the boundary, with concatenation in the first coordinate. Call a continuous map a weak homotopy equivalence when it induces a bijection on path components and an isomorphism on every $\pi_n$ at every source basepoint. Let $h:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of arbitrary topological spaces and let $U,V\subseteq Y$ be open subsets with $Y=U\cup V$. Give all subsets their subspace topologies. If the three restrictions $$h:h^{-1}(U)\to U,\qquad h:h^{-1}(V)\to V,\qquad h:h^{-1}(U\cap V)\to U\cap V$$ are weak homotopy equivalences, then $h:X\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No separation, compact-generation or connectedness hypothesis is imposed, and empty spaces and empty intersections are allowed.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent middle derived adjunction: generic topological gluing input for the realization-singular comparison of double mapping cylinders. This technical input is not asserted in the blueprint paragraph itself. Agent-formulated arbitrary-space binary-open-cover version. Related external reference read online: J. P. May, A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology, Chapter 10, section 7, final theorem, printed pp. 80-82, https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/CONCISE/ConciseRevised.pdf . May imposes compact-generation conventions in Chapter 5; his theorem is not claimed verbatim for arbitrary spaces here. An archived reference for the precise arbitrary-space version is WANTED. No Stacks tag is claimed.

proof.text: For a space $Z$ and an open subset $W$, write $S_Z(W)$ for the singular subcomplex consisting of simplices whose image lies in $W$. Apply [lem-coef-open-cover-singular-excision] to the cover $Y=U\cup V$ and to the induced open cover $X=h^{-1}(U)\cup h^{-1}(V)$. We obtain weak equivalences $e_Y:S_Y(U)\amalg_{S_Y(U\cap V)}S_Y(V)\to\operatorname{Sing}(Y)$ and $e_X:S_X(h^{-1}U)\amalg_{S_X(h^{-1}(U\cap V))}S_X(h^{-1}V)\to\operatorname{Sing}(X)$. The preimages are open because $h$ is continuous, and the cover and empty cases are exactly those allowed by the excision statement.

source.place: Chapter 10, §7, final excision theorem; singular-complex formulation.

proof.text: For each of the three restricted maps $r:h^{-1}(W)\to W$ with $W=U,V,U\cap V$, naturality of the evaluation maps gives $\varepsilon_W\circ|\operatorname{Sing}(r)|=r\circ\varepsilon_{h^{-1}(W)}$. Both evaluation maps are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-singular-counit-weak-equivalence], while $r$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by hypothesis. Cancellation in the induced bijections on components and homotopy-group isomorphisms makes $|\operatorname{Sing}(r)|$ a weak homotopy equivalence. By [lem-cbc-realization-weak-equivalence], this is precisely the weak-equivalence notion for the corresponding simplicial maps. Thus the three component maps between the singular subcomplex spans are weak equivalences.

source.place: Chapter 10, §7, naturality of singular realization and excision comparison.

proof.text:
The maps $S_X(h^{-1}(U\cap V))\to S_X(h^{-1}U)$ and $S_Y(U\cap V)\to S_Y(U)$ are inclusions of simplicial subsets, hence monomorphisms. The component maps in Step 2 form a commuting map of the two spans. Apply the pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] to obtain a weak homotopy equivalence
$$p:S_X(h^{-1}U)\amalg_{S_X(h^{-1}(U\cap V))}S_X(h^{-1}V)\longrightarrow S_Y(U)\amalg_{S_Y(U\cap V)}S_Y(V).$$

source.place: Chapter 10, §7, excision map of singular subcomplexes; simplicial pushout invariance supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: Naturality of singular subcomplexes gives a strictly commutative square $e_Y\circ p=\operatorname{Sing}(h)\circ e_X$. The maps $e_X$, $e_Y$ and $p$ are weak homotopy equivalences by Steps 1 and 3, so cancellation on components and on every based homotopy group shows that $\operatorname{Sing}(h):\operatorname{Sing}(X)\to\operatorname{Sing}(Y)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The empty cases are covered: if a source or target singular set is empty, the same square and the component bijection criterion apply.

source.place: Chapter 10, §7, final comparison and two-out-of-three argument.

proof.text: The evaluation maps again give a strictly commutative square $\varepsilon_Y\circ|\operatorname{Sing}(h)|=h\circ\varepsilon_X$. The two evaluation maps are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-singular-counit-weak-equivalence], and $|\operatorname{Sing}(h)|$ is one by Step 4. Cancelling the component bijections and homotopy-group isomorphisms in this square proves that $h$ is a weak homotopy equivalence in the cubical sense stated in the item. No separation, compact-generation or connectedness hypothesis was introduced.

source.place: Chapter 10, §7, naturality and final weak-equivalence conclusion.
